results.title: Results
results.description: A dictionary mapping RP entity IDs to lists of event calendar entries for each company. Only events whose company has an rp_entity_id appear here; the rest are in 'events_unmapped', so read both to get the whole calendar.

events_unmapped.title: Events Unmapped
events_unmapped.description: Events whose company has not been mapped to an rp_entity_id appear here instead of in 'results'. For an IPO listing this reflects a temporary state in the mapping process: once the company begins trading and mapping completes, the event moves into 'results'. A delisted company may instead never have been mapped. Identify these events by 'ticker' and 'company_name'.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: The content catalog sources the response was built from, one entry per source. Empty when no catalog source contributed.

usage.description: Tokens the request consumed, per content tier. Present only for API keys billed in tokens.

category.title: Category
category.description: The category of the event, such as 'earnings-call' or 'conference-call'.

event_datetime.title: Event Datetime
event_datetime.description: The date and time of the event in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-12-05T20:00:00Z'). Events whose source dates them to the day rather than to the minute, such as IPO listings and delistings, are reported at midnight UTC on that date.

title.title: Title
title.description: The title of the event, which provides a brief description of the event's content.

fiscal_year.title: Fiscal Year
fiscal_year.description: The fiscal year of the event.

fiscal_period.title: Fiscal Period
fiscal_period.description: The fiscal period of the event, such as 'Q1', 'Q2', etc.

rp_collection_id.title: Rp Collection Id
rp_collection_id.description: The RP collection id. All RP documents can be fetched using this id. Absent for events with no document behind them, such as IPO listings and delistings.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: The date and time when the event data was last updated, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-02-27T09:35:45Z').

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: The date and time when the event data was created, in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-11-15T08:14:26Z').

ticker.title: Ticker
ticker.description: The ticker the company trades, or traded, under. IPO listings and delistings only.

company_name.title: Company Name
company_name.description: The company name as the source reports it. IPO listings and delistings only.

exchange.title: Exchange
exchange.description: The exchange the company listed on, or was delisted from, as the source names it (e.g. 'NASDAQ'). IPO listings and delistings only. This is the source's own name, not a MIC code, and neither category can be filtered by exchange at all: setting the 'exchanges' request filter excludes both from the response.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: Next page token or URL to retrieve the next page of results.

has_cursor.title: Has Cursor
has_cursor.description: Whether there are more pages available after this one.

Pagination.title: Pagination
Pagination.description: Common pagination response for endpoints that support pagination.

id.title: Id
id.description: Content catalog identifier of the source.

name.title: Name
name.description: Catalog name of the dataset the data came from.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: A content catalog source that contributed data to a structured-data response.

Usage.title: Usage
Usage.description:
Public structured-data usage for a request, aggregated per content tier.

A flat object keyed per content tier, where each key is derived from the
content tier identifier by dropping the ``content-`` prefix and appending
``_tokens`` (e.g. ``corporate-fundamentals`` ->
``corporate_fundamentals_tokens``). It is sparse: only tiers with non-zero
tokens appear, and an absent key means zero tokens for that tier.
